about.title: Soledad Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Soledad's economy runs on a mix of agriculture, warehousing, and local commercial corridors along Front Street and Monterey Street, and each of those settings carries its own injury risks. When a worker gets hurt on the job here, California law usually routes the claim through workers' compensation, no matter who was at fault. But that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, a piece of defective equipment, a property owner, or someone outside your employer caused or contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside the comp claim. This matters for Soledad workers because agricultural and industrial sites often involve multiple contractors and equipment vendors, any of whom might bear some responsibility. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect injured workers with an independent attorney, free of charge, who can look at the specifics of a Soledad workplace injury and explain the realistic options.

whyChoose.title: Why Soledad Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Help Identify Third-Party Options
items.desc: Because workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, many injured workers never realize a negligent third party, like an equipment maker or subcontractor, could still be liable. The attorney you're connected with can evaluate whether a separate claim applies to your situation.

items.title: Understanding of Reporting Deadlines
items.desc: California requires injured workers to report the incident to their employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate a claim. We help make sure you're connected quickly with someone who can guide you through next steps.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation Is the Law
items.desc: Retaliation against a worker for reporting an injury is illegal in California. The attorney you speak with can explain your rights if you're worried about how reporting an injury might affect your job.

items.question: Can I still file a claim if my employer says my injury doesn't qualify for workers' comp?
items.answer: Employers sometimes dispute claims, but that doesn't automatically mean you have no options. An independent attorney can review the facts of your case, including whether a third party contributed to the injury, and explain what avenues may be available. LawProactive can connect you with that attorney at no cost.

items.question: I work at a Soledad packing or agricultural site and got hurt using rented equipment. Does that change anything?
items.answer: It might. While your claim against your employer typically goes through workers' comp, if the equipment was owned, maintained, or supplied by a separate company, that company could potentially be held liable in a third-party claim. This is common in Monterey County agricultural work, and it's worth having an attorney look closely at who was involved.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a third-party claim after a workplace injury in Soledad?
items.answer: Third-party injury claims in California generally carry a two-year deadline from the date of the injury. This is separate from the workers' comp reporting window, so it helps to get guidance early. LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who can walk through the relevant timelines for your situation.
